title: Mental Health in University/Work: A Personal Safety Net
summary: Your teen's move to university or work brings new pressures: being away from home, performance, relationships, and financial decisions. Help them build their tools: (1) A steady routine for sleep, movement and meals — the foundation of brain health. (2) A support network: a trusted friend, an academic mentor, a university counsellor, and your country's mental-health helpline saved on their phone. (3) Personal warning signs they write down and monitor weekly. (4) An emergency plan: your country's emergency number, a friend they can turn to, and a psychiatrist they know. Independence means learning to look after their own mental health, with you behind them.
try_this: This week: Sit with your teen and write a personal "safety card" together: 3 warning signs, 3 ways to calm down, 3 people they trust, and your country's emergency number. They should keep it in their wallet or on their phone.
reflection_prompts: What are the three warning signs your teen identified?
Who are the three people in their safety net?
